contract.notes: Durable, pluggable stores with reference in-memory implementations for tests. Consume-once and compare-and-swap are required operations, not conventions: replay handling and single-flight refresh depend on them.

stores.name: TransactionStore
stores.notes: Encrypted PKCE verifier is never logged.

stores.name: AuthorizationCodeStore
atomicity: the record is retained after consume so a replay is distinguishable from an unknown code
stores.notes: Holds no unencrypted upstream material. encrypted_token_response (the upstream TokenSet, encrypted) embeds the upstream-minted access token and is permitted, so the code exchange can return the access token byte-for-byte unmodified; the durable upstream refresh token is written to the broker record.
stores.replay_behaviour: replay returns invalid_grant and revokes the broker record the code minted

stores.name: RouteRefreshBrokerStore
stores.ttl: <= min(upstream refresh lifetime, route/session lifetime, local policy)
stores.notes: SEP-2352: a handle is never rebound to a new issuer or client registration; the broker upstream issuer stays the stage upstream issuer while the client-facing route issuer is the route URL.

stores.name: RateLimitStore
stores.notes: Per-route buckets for DCR and legacy adoption; a store failure fails closed when the app requires it.

reference_implementations.purpose: deterministic tests and local development only
reference_implementations.durability: production implementations are application-owned (e.g. TableTheory/DynamoDB in TMS/Autheory)

single_flight_refresh.coalesce_wait_bound: framework default, app-overridable; must be < lock ttl
single_flight_refresh.grace_window: framework default, app-overridable; must exceed the wait bound and not exceed the lock ttl
behaviour: winner performs the upstream refresh and writes the grace response
concurrent callers receive the winner's grace response without a second upstream call
the upstream leg presents the client that owns the recorded upstream material
rotation atomically replaces the encrypted upstream material under a versioned compare-and-swap
transient contention returns a retryable 503 with Retry-After, never invalid_grant
only an explicit upstream stale/replaced marks reauth_required
